3

Details

The old narrative arc in PAPER_STATUS was: sharing measured → it breaks time-based tracking → unsharing and a geometry estimator fix it → the hybrid makes it uniform → sharing repaid as sub-pitch position. The waveform-first forward model absorbs the middle three steps, and the hybrid tracker is superseded (it should appear, if at all, as the motivation).

The proposed arc leads with the physics of the resistive layer, measured directly in the beam, then the reconstruction that models it, then the performance it gives on cosmics, with the SPS intrinsic resolution as the anchor. Gas and operations follow.

The ordering of §2 before §4 matters: the beam measurement is what justifies the kernel ordering the cosmic reconstruction ships with.

Details

Retired means the topic disappears as a paper section: the forward model does what the unsharing correction and the hybrid regression approximated. They can be mentioned as what the hits chain needed.

Open, in priority order for next week: (8) run the six det3 drift-scan rows locally on r06 (they need the hits-chain alignment and event cache, so they cannot go to condor); (10) port the time resolution to waveforms; (5) re-measure the edge angle tilt with wft angles; (7) PLAN_40's three skeptic tests; (1) quote the SPS kernel instead of the hits sharing constants.

Two more things the cosmic-performance text must handle: det6's X plane is not dead (the old table says it is; wft gives σ_θ 2.2°), and det4's poor bench numbers come from 62 % of its area not amplifying, in fixed ~35 mm stripes (sps_beam_test_26/det4_sps_assessment/).

Waveform-first improves σ_θ on every plane

σ_θ per plane against the M3 reference, golden run per detector, r06 calibration (det4: lp_t0p, det6: lp).

hits chain

waveform-first, r06

Solid bars are the X plane, pale bars Y.

Every plane improves, by ×1.03 to ×2.2: halved on det3, least on det6 Y and det4 Y. The bias is consistent with zero everywhere.

The improvement is not a tuning gain: the hits chain is biased by construction, and the forward model removes the bias.

det3 and det2 are the headline chambers; det6 and det7 carry board-C/D sharing; det4 is gain-limited and better shown through SPS.

Source: mx_june_wft/FLEET_DIGEST.md (r06 promotion, 2026-08-19).

Details

Source: mx_june_wft/FLEET_DIGEST.md (written by mx_june_wft/digest.py, last committed 2026-08-19 with the r06 promotion), which compares both chains on the same events with the same M3 recipe (χ² < 1, NClus = 4).

The bundles differ by detector: r06 (c2 = 0.6 c1) on det2, det3 and det7; calib_bundle_lp_t0p on det4 and calib_bundle_lp on det6, whose ratios were already below 1. Columns built on different bundles are not interchangeable; the paper table has to say which bundle each row used.

The r06 cost, from the paired bootstrap in R06_GATE_2026-08-19.md: det3 Y +0.06°, det7 X +0.08°, det7 Y +0.13° relative to the inverted kernel. The data prefer the inverted kernel inside this model; the proposed per-plane ratio is the identified fix and has not been built.

6

Details

Gains in points of within-5 mm: det4 +21, det6 +17, det7 +14. det3 and det2 were already at ~92–93 % and stay there. det4's low value is its geometry: 62 % of its active area does not amplify, in fixed stripes (DET4_SPS_ASSESSMENT.md).

All residuals here are detector ⊕ reference. The next slide is why the bench cannot measure the chamber's intrinsic position resolution, and what does.

Spark fractions in the same digest (det3 8 %, det2 10 %, det4 10 %, det6 22 %, det7 37 %) are identical between chains, as they should be: detection is still hits-defined.

det4 resolves 176 µm; the bench sees its reference

det4 in SPS H4, run 53, 44,198 tracks at normal incidence, by uRWELL zone (view, pitch in mm).

residual to the uRWELL

det4, reference removed

bench

The uRWELL back plane has three pitches, so the reference’s own term is fitted out, not modelled: det4 = 176 µm = 0.30 × pitch.

The bench reference points with a core σ of 0.21/0.24 mm, without scattering. ~1.1 mrad over 558 mm adds 614 µm and closes the bench residual.

PLAN_37 asked for this deconvolution. The beam answers it, but the scattering term is inferred, not measured.

7

Details

Source: sps_beam_test_26/analysis/spatial_resolution/ (resolution.py → results.json; report report.html). The five zones are independent: three uRWELL pitches on X, two on Y. The joint fit over the back plane's pitches gives σ_det4 = 176 ± 10 µm with χ² = 2.8.

The bench bar is arithmetic: 176 µm ⊕ the M3 pointing core (quadrature mean of 0.21 and 0.24 mm, from the M3 self-resolution study, which excludes multiple scattering by construction) ⊕ 1.1 mrad × 558 mm. The SPS report's own caveat: the scattering explanation is arithmetic, not a measurement. A paper would want either a scattering simulation of the bench stack or the M3 inter-doublet kink (2.6 mrad measured) used directly.

Caveat for the paper: this is det4 at normal incidence in its live bands, in Ar/CF₄/iso. It establishes what the chamber design can do, not det3's number at cosmic angles.

Beam: c2/c1 = 0.45; every retired bundle had c2 > c1

Sharing ratio c2/c1: the retired bundles, the shipped one, and the two direct measurements.

Head-on in the beam, the cross-relation n₀∗W_d = n_d∗W₀ cancels the unknown drive signal, so the kernel is measured with no deconvolution.

c2/c1 = 0.42–0.47 at three drift fields; det3 bench cosmics agree within errors. Every shipped bundle before 8-19 sat on the wrong side of 1.

The ±1 delay is 49 ns on the flat mount and survives a 25.6° rotation.

8

Details

Sources: sps_beam_test_26/analysis/sharing_kernel/fit_kernel.json (beam, Y view, delay form fitted on RAW run 71 at 243/156/95 V/cm) and bench_kernel_y.json (det3 near-vertical cosmics, tan θ < 0.05). Retired ratios from mx_june_wft/RETIRE_C2GTC1_2026-08-21.md §2. Errors are the fits' bootstrap errors.

What the beam did not pin: the absolute time constant walks 629 → 1040 ns as the fit window grows, because 44–52 % of the central-strip amplitude is still present at the last sample. τ and c2 are bounds. The cascade (lp) form fits the cross-relation at 2.1 % residual against the shipped delay form's 4.2 %, but transplanted onto det3 it costs σ_θ(Y) 1.14 → 1.54°, so it is not adopted.

The cosmic χ² prefers c2 ≥ c1 inside the current model (R06_GATE). The paper should present that as evidence about the model, with the beam as the arbiter.

On lxplus, ~/wft_campaign holds the pre-fix 8-13 tarballs and ~/wft_campaign_r06 the 8-21 re-run; /eos/user/d/dneff/x17 has no wft campaign output.

Bundles named in FLEET_DIGEST: det3 r06, det2 r06, det4 lp_t0p, det6 lp, det7 r06.

The campaign packager has two known traps (RETIRE_C2GTC1_2026-08-21.md §6a–6b): it ran det4 without the t0 prior once ("t0p-adopted dets: none yet" is the tell), and a v-refit seeded from an r06 bundle used to write c2 = 0 with no ratio (fixed, tested). Expect bit-identity on det2/3/4/6; det7 differed on 3 of 8,082 events.

What this does not rule out

The bench resolution is not decomposed

The scattering term behind the bench residual is inferred arithmetic. A bench-stack scattering simulation or the measured M3 kink would make it a result.

One calibration, one model

r06 is better physics and a worse fit (Y up to +0.13°). The per-plane ratio and the lp-vs-delay branch are both unresolved and both would re-open the gates.

The kernel tail is outside every window

τ and c2 are bounds. No beam for three years.

Golden runs only

One run per detector is reconstructed to paper standard; HV-scan rows are stamped off-conditions (trend grade).

det4 speaks through SPS

62 % of its area does not amplify; its bench numbers are geometry.

Decisions before writing

Freeze r06 as it stands?

Or build the per-plane ratio first. Write on r06 unless the ratio is a few days’ work.

Which chambers in the main table

det3 + det2 headline; det6/7 as the board-C/D contrast; det4 via SPS.

Journal

NIM A or JINST: length and figure budget follow from it.
